purpose: Add observational/cohort human evidence to reduce RCT-only bias in the Gold Corpus.
source_policy: All records correspond to verified PubMed records. Evidence text is curator-written from the PubMed abstract and explicitly not verbatim.
overlap_policy: PMIDs are unique and disjoint from all human-evidence JSON datasets present in the validated repository including Extension 02.

records.title: St John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum) Fresh Plant Tincture for Patients with Mild to Moderate Depression: A Prospective Observational Study
records.evidence_text: In this prospective observational cohort, depressive symptom scores declined substantially over six weeks and responder rates were comparable with reference trials of high-dose St John's wort extracts.

records.title: Garlic Consumption and All-Cause Mortality among Chinese Oldest-Old Individuals: A Population-Based Cohort Study
records.evidence_text: Habitual garlic consumption was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality, with lower adjusted mortality hazards among occasional and frequent users than rare users.

records.title: Consumption of sweetened, dried cranberries may reduce urinary tract infection incidence in susceptible women--a modified observational study
records.evidence_text: The mean six-month UTI rate decreased significantly after sweetened dried cranberry consumption, and the study concluded that cranberry consumption had a beneficial effect on recurrent UTI incidence.

records.title: Black cohosh with or without St. John's wort for symptom-specific climacteric treatment--results of a large-scale, controlled, observational study
records.evidence_text: Both black cohosh regimens improved menopausal symptom measures in routine practice, with the combination regimen producing a significantly greater improvement in the psychological symptom score.

records.title: Green tea consumption and mortality due to cardiovascular disease, cancer, and all causes in Japan: the Ohsaki study
records.evidence_text: Higher green tea consumption was associated with reduced all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in this large prospective cohort.

records.title: Association of green tea consumption with mortality from all-cause, cardiovascular disease and cancer in a Chinese cohort of 165,000 adult men
records.evidence_text: Green tea consumption was associated with lower risk of mortality from all causes and cardiovascular disease in this large cohort.

records.title: Effect of coffee and green tea consumption on the risk of liver cancer: cohort analysis by hepatitis virus infection status
records.evidence_text: Green tea consumption was not associated with a reduced risk of liver cancer in the prospective cohort.

records.title: Green tea and coffee intake and risk of pancreatic cancer in a large-scale, population-based cohort study in Japan (JPHC study)
records.evidence_text: Overall pancreatic cancer risk was not associated with green tea intake in this large population-based cohort.

records.title: Coffee, Green Tea, and Caffeine Intake and Liver Cancer Risk: A Prospective Cohort Study
records.evidence_text: No association between green tea intake and liver cancer risk was observed during the prospective follow-up.

records.title: Similar treatment outcomes with Ginkgo biloba extract EGb 761 and donepezil in Alzheimer's dementia in very old age: A retrospective observational study
records.clinical_context: Alzheimer dementia in adults aged 80 years or older
records.evidence_text: Cognitive decline did not differ significantly between Ginkgo extract and donepezil, while adverse events were less frequent with Ginkgo.

records.title: Association between ginseng intake and mortality: Kangwha cohort study
records.evidence_text: Ginseng intake was associated with lower all-cause mortality in older men, but no corresponding all-cause mortality association was observed in women and cardiovascular mortality was not related to ginseng intake.

records.title: Black cohosh (Cimicifuga racemosa) in tamoxifen-treated breast cancer patients with climacteric complaints - a prospective observational study
records.evidence_text: Hot flashes, sweating, sleep problems and anxiety improved during black cohosh treatment, whereas urogenital and musculoskeletal complaints did not change.
